A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion for System 2 Planning. All 20 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original maze-navigation, cube-manipulation, and visual-planning experiments, including success rates, runtime measurements, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–3 and 8–9, Figure 6, and the accompanying analyses.

M1.justification: The tree-structured denoising procedure, guidance meta-actions, jumpy simulation, model architecture, and task-specific adaptations are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A, B, and D.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same pointmaze and antmaze navigation tasks, short-horizon pointmaze stitch datasets, one-to-four-cube manipulation tasks, and partially observable visual pointmaze environments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Diffuser, its replanning and random-search variants, Diffusion Forcing, and the goal-inpainting Diffuser comparisons in Table 9.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same task configurations, preprocessing, planning horizons, controllers, training settings, success-rate metric, and denoising-budget evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The compute-budget study in Figure 6, cube-plan entanglement examples in Figure 4, and visual trajectory-collapse analysis in Figure 7 and Appendix A.7.7 are unchanged. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 identically reports evaluation with 10 random seeds per model for each of five tasks per environment. Both versions retain the same mean and standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 1–3 and 8–9 and Figure 6. For example, MCTD remains at 100 ± 0% on giant pointmaze navigation and 82 ± 18% on medium visual pointmaze.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations (1)–(7) and the DDIM update in Algorithm 9 are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim about explicit four-stage MCTS integration, the same three central innovations, and the same claims about planning performance and test-time compute scalability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exploration, replanning, local-control failures, and visual-planning difficulties are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same computational-cost limitations and proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B, and D preserve the same hyperparameters, guidance sets, model and controller details, pseudocode, and code-source links. No reproducibility or resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 4 and Appendix C's comparison with Monte Carlo Guidance. The reference list is identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds New York University as an affiliation for Sungjin Ahn and updates the arXiv version/date marking. The substantive prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer affiliation footnote produces column and page reflow in the main text, shifting paragraph and heading positions. Figures, tables, captions, and their contents remain unchanged; pages 9–20 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 adds affiliation information and changes main-text layout, while preserving all scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility details, including the appendices. These administrative and layout changes establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
